> DRAFT written in `projects/storage-schema/drafts/`. Not submitted. The reference implementation is in this project. Numbers marked [M] were measured by `scripts/build-demos.sh` and are in `fixtures/size-report.json`.

## Simple Summary

A contract MAY carry a description of its storage (which keys it writes, with what durability, and what value types) in a Wasm custom section named `contractstoragev0`. The section is separate from the callable interface in `contractspecv0`. Off-chain tools use it to turn raw contract-data ledger entries into named, typed records. It never affects execution.

## Dependencies

- SEP-48 (Contract Interface Specification): this SEP reuses `SCSpecTypeDef`, `SCSpecEntry` and the custom-section conventions of `contractspecv0`.
- `SCVal`, `ContractDataEntry` and `ContractDataDurability` from `Stellar-contract.x` / `Stellar-ledger-entries.x`.

## Motivation

Contract storage keys and values are untyped `SCVal`s. An indexer, explorer, wallet or Lab that sees a contract-data entry cannot name it or check its type without the contract's source. Symptoms in Stellar repos: Lab's storage tab error (laboratory#2175), `stellar contract read --key` accepting only symbols (stellar-cli#2041), indexers special-casing tokens (wallet-backend#610, stellar-etl#354).

Two things are settled in rs-soroban-sdk#1818:

- Storage types should not be in the contract spec: they are an implementation detail, and the spec is the callable interface.
- A separate place "is interesting", possibly "in the contract wasm file but in a custom section separated from the contract specs" (leighmcculloch, 2026-04-27).

The open question from that thread is answered in [Mapping ledger entries](#mapping-ledger-entries-to-schema-entries) below.

Since soroban-sdk 28, spec shaking removes types that are not reachable from functions or events, so storage-only types are absent from `contractspecv0` even when a contract would like to publish them. This SEP carries them.

## Abstract

This SEP defines:

1. a custom section `contractstoragev0` holding a stream of `SCStorageEntry` values: key entries (durability, key pattern, value type) and type entries (UDT definitions);
2. a deterministic procedure that maps a contract-data ledger entry to at most one schema entry, or reports it as `unknown` or `ambiguous`;
3. an equivalent JSON sidecar for contracts that cannot or will not embed the section, such as the built-in Stellar Asset Contract.

The section is informational. It does not mandate a storage layout. A contract without it, or with a partial one, is valid.

## Specification

### Section

- Name: `contractstoragev0`.
- Content: zero or more XDR-encoded `SCStorageEntry` values, concatenated, with no header or length prefix.
- A module MAY contain several sections with this name. Readers MUST concatenate them in module order. Linkers merge same-name `#[link_section]` data, and a post-build tool can append a section.
- Readers MUST reject a stream that does not decode completely.
- Readers MUST drop exact duplicate entries. Two different definitions of one type name are a conflict: readers keep the first by precedence (below) and SHOULD warn.

### XDR

```
enum SCStorageEntryKind { SC_STORAGE_ENTRY_KEY_V0 = 0, SC_STORAGE_ENTRY_TYPE_V0 = 1 };

// Extends ContractDataDurability (TEMPORARY = 0, PERSISTENT = 1).
enum SCStorageDurability { SC_STORAGE_TEMPORARY = 0, SC_STORAGE_PERSISTENT = 1, SC_STORAGE_INSTANCE = 2 };

enum SCStorageKeyKind { SC_STORAGE_KEY_EXACT = 0, SC_STORAGE_KEY_TAGGED = 1, SC_STORAGE_KEY_TYPED = 2 };

struct SCStorageKeyFieldV0 { string name<30>; SCSpecTypeDef type; };
struct SCStorageKeyTaggedV0 { string tag<32>; SCStorageKeyFieldV0 fields<>; };

union SCStorageKey switch (SCStorageKeyKind kind) {
case SC_STORAGE_KEY_EXACT:  SCVal exact;
case SC_STORAGE_KEY_TAGGED: SCStorageKeyTaggedV0 tagged;
case SC_STORAGE_KEY_TYPED:  SCSpecTypeDef typed;
};

struct SCStorageKeyEntryV0 {
    string doc<1024>;
    string lib<80>;      // who writes the entry: "" = the contract; otherwise crate[@version]
    string name<60>;     // display name, e.g. "DataKey::Balance"
    SCStorageDurability durability;
    SCStorageKey key;
    SCSpecTypeDef value;
};

union SCStorageEntry switch (SCStorageEntryKind kind) {
case SC_STORAGE_ENTRY_KEY_V0:  SCStorageKeyEntryV0 keyV0;
case SC_STORAGE_ENTRY_TYPE_V0: SCSpecEntry typeV0;   // a UDT, encoded exactly as in contractspecv0
};
```

### Mapping ledger entries to schema entries

Input: a `ContractDataEntry` `(contract, key, durability, val)` and the schema of the code the contract instance currently runs.

1. **Instance expansion.** If `key` is `SCV_LEDGER_KEY_CONTRACT_INSTANCE`, each element `(k, v)` of `val.instance.storage` is decoded as a separate entry with durability `INSTANCE`. Otherwise the durability is the entry's `ContractDataDurability`.
2. **Candidates.** Schema entry `E` is a candidate when `E.durability` equals the entry's durability and:
   - `EXACT(v)`: `key == v`.
   - `TAGGED(tag, f1..fn)`: `key` is an `SCV_VEC` of length `n + 1` whose first element is `SCV_SYMBOL(tag)` and whose element `i` conforms to `fi.type`. This is the encoding `#[contracttype]` gives enum variants (a unit variant is `[Symbol(tag)]`) and the encoding of `(Symbol(namespace), k1, ..)` tuple keys.
   - `TYPED(t)`: `key` conforms to `t`.
3. **Specificity.** Keep only the candidates of the highest kind: `EXACT` > `TAGGED` > `TYPED`.
4. **Result.**
   - No candidate: `unknown`.
   - One candidate: `matched` if `val` conforms to `E.value`, otherwise `value_mismatch`.
   - More than one: `ambiguous`. The decoder lists every candidate with whether its value type conforms, and MUST NOT silently choose.

Conformance follows the soroban value encoding:

- A named struct is a map with exactly its field symbols. A tuple struct is a vec.
- A union is `[Symbol(case), ..]`. An integer enum is `SCV_U32` with a declared value.
- `Option<T>` is `SCV_VOID` or `T`. `BytesN<n>` is bytes of length `n`. `Val` is anything.
- A referenced type with no definition conforms to anything, and the decoder MUST warn.

Type definitions are looked up first in `contractstoragev0` type entries, then in sidecars, then in `contractspecv0`.

Hard cases, stated plainly:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Raw symbol keys (`symbol_short!("COUNTER")`) | `EXACT(Symbol)` |
| Instance storage | per-element decode, durability `INSTANCE`, TTL of the instance |
| Keys written by a dependency | declared with `lib = "crate@version"`, either by the dependency's own section or by the contract on its behalf |
| Same key under two durabilities | different ledger entries. Durability is part of the match (OpenZeppelin stellar-contracts v0.8.0 relies on this for its total-supply migration) |
| Two declarations with the same key shape and durability (rs-soroban-sdk#2088) | one ledger entry, so `ambiguous` with evidence. No schema can resolve this after the fact. Tools SHOULD lint for it before deploy |
| Entries written by earlier code after an upgrade | `value_mismatch` or `unknown`. History-aware decoding needs the code active at the entry's last modification, and is out of scope for v0 |

### Sidecar JSON

The same model as JSON (field names in the reference JSON Schema). Value and field types are written in Rust syntax as mapped by `#[contracttype]`, for example `"Map<Address, i128>"`. Type definitions are written as Rust source or as `SCSpecEntry` JSON. A sidecar can be injected into a wasm before deploy (producing a section byte-identical to an embedded one), or given to a decoder directly. The latter is the only option for the built-in Stellar Asset Contract.

## Design Rationale

- **Separate section, not the spec.** It follows #1818: the callable interface stays clean, and the storage description travels with the code hash.
- **Patterns, not a key list.** Storage keys are parameterised (`Balance(Address)`). A schema has to describe families of keys, and `TAGGED` mirrors the one encoding the SDK actually produces.
- **Durability in the match.** It is part of the ledger key, so it is free to use, and it disambiguates real cases.
- **Honest statuses.** A decoder that guesses would mislabel #2088 collisions and post-upgrade data. `ambiguous` and `value_mismatch` make those visible instead.
- **Type entries.** Spec shaking means a storage schema cannot assume its types are in `contractspecv0`. Reusing the `SCSpecEntry` encoding lets SDK macros emit the bytes they already compute (`spec_xdr()`).
- **Opt-in and informational.** Nothing changes for contracts that do not use it. This also answers the objection that internal types should not appear in an external ABI: the section is not the ABI, tools that do not want it ignore it, and a contract can ship the schema as a sidecar instead of in the wasm.
- **Size.** The section adds bytes to the uploaded wasm and nothing else. Measured [M] on the reference demos (soroban-sdk 28.0.0, release profile): see the table in "Implementations". The code sections are byte-identical with and without the section. Contracts that care about every byte can use a sidecar and pay nothing on-chain.

## Security Concerns

- The section is a claim by the contract author, not a proof. A malicious or careless schema can mislabel entries. Decoders MUST treat it as untrusted input: bound allocation, reject malformed streams, and keep raw XDR next to every decoded value.
- The section is covered by the wasm hash, so a schema read from a deployed contract's code cannot be changed without changing the code. A sidecar has no such binding. Tools SHOULD show which source a decoding came from.
- Nothing in this SEP affects authorization, execution or fees beyond the upload size of the section.

## Implementations

Reference implementation (Rust, Apache-2.0), in the user's repository:

- Format, sidecar, decoder, lint and read-only RPC fetch: `sik-storage-schema-core`.
- `#[storage_schema]` / `#[storage_key]` / `storage_schema_extern!` emitters: `sik-storage-schema-macros`.
- CLI `storage-schema` (`inspect`, `inject`, `strip`, `lint`, `decode`, `key`, `size`).
- Demos: soroban-examples `token` and `increment` annotated with the macro; OpenZeppelin stellar-contracts v0.8.0 `fungible-pausable` unmodified, with a sidecar injected post-build; mainnet USDC Stellar Asset Contract entries decoded through a sidecar.

Measured section cost [M] (from `fixtures/size-report.json`):

| Contract (soroban-sdk 28.0.0, release) | Keys | Type entries | Section bytes | Module bytes (shaken, `stellar contract build`) | Section as share of that module (the module already contains it) | Code identical to no-schema build |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| soroban-examples `token` (macro) | 4 | 3 | 885 | 8,885 (7,674 with `--optimize`) | 10.0% (11.5% optimised) | yes (raw `cargo rustc` pair 12,800 vs 11,915 B; delta = 885) |
| soroban-examples `increment` (macro) | 1 | 0 | 72 | 747 | 9.6% | yes (raw pair 3,919 vs 3,847 B; delta = 72) |
| OZ v0.8.0 `fungible-pausable` (sidecar injected post-build) | 7 | 3 | 1,273 | 13,814 (12,541 before inject) | 9.2% | yes (strip restores the original bytes) |

Cost is the section bytes and nothing else. About 75-110 B per key entry plus each embedded type definition [M, 2026-11-03, `fixtures/size-report.json`; per-key figure is an [I] from these three rows]. Soroban's maximum contract size and per-byte upload fees apply to these bytes [U: fee per byte not computed here].
